title: Ruling on Men Wearing Gold Rings
summary: Men are prohibited from wearing gold rings in Islam; only silver is allowed.
translation: Can men wear a gold ring or not? This question often arises, so men should remember that only wearing a silver ring is permissible and that too should weigh four grams and 3.47 (4.347) grams only. Moreover, there is no harm in setting it with a diamond or an ornament. Rings made of gold, iron, brass, or other metals are prohibited for men. Many people question why gold is not permissible for men while it is for women. The primary point to understand is that if we are given a command through the Holy Prophet (PBUH) or directly by Allah, that is sufficient for us. The prohibition of using gold is explicitly mentioned in the blessed hadith. Therefore, a believer accepts religious rulings as Allah’s command, whether the wisdom behind it is understood or not. It is true every ruling in Shariah is based on wisdom and benefit, but it is not necessary to act only when one grasps the wisdom. Acting on rulings due to the command of the Prophet (PBUH) or Shariah is sufficient. It is narrated in Abu Dawood that the Prophet (PBUH) once came out holding silk in one hand and gold in the other and said, 'These two are forbidden for the men of my Ummah and permissible for its women.' As for the objectives of the Shariah, scholars explain that decoration and adornment through gold are inappropriate for men, which is why Shariah forbids it. In contrast, for women, beauty is intended to attract the husband, hence the leniency in their case.
